title: Trump reverses rally cancellations, announces Kansas trip ahead of midterms
content: Candidates make last‑minute pitches ahead of Tuesday's midterms; economy weighs heavily on voters' minds. With just days to go before the midterm elections, Republicans and Democrats are making their final case to voters to turn out at the polls on Nov. 3. President Trump made a surprise reversal this week after his last‑minute decision to cancel rallies in battleground states, announcing a day later he would travel to Kansas.
summary: Republicans and Democrats are making their final case to voters to turn out at the polls on Nov. 3. President Trump reversed his decision to cancel rallies in battleground states and announced a trip to Kansas.
author: The Hill

title: 5 State Supreme Court Races to Watch on Tuesday
content: Voters in half the country will decide who sits on state Supreme Courts next Tuesday. State Supreme Court races appear on ballots in two dozen states this November, including partisan, nonpartisan, and retention contests that decide which candidates win seats or remain on the bench of courts that often have the final word.
summary: Voters in half of the country will decide who sits on the bench of their state’s highest court next Tuesday. State Supreme Court races are on ballot in two dozen states this November, with partisan, nonpartisan and retention contests determining which candidates win seats or remain on the bench.
author: The Hill

title: Mike Rogers says he's about 7% ahead on early-returned ballots in Michigan Senate race
content: Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers stated he is ahead by nearly seven percent on early-returned ballots, a claim that contradicts recent polls favoring his Democratic opponent, Abdul El-Sayed. Rogers made the assertion during a public appearance, citing internal models regarding voters he believes are supporting his campaign.
summary: Michigan Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers claimed he is ahead by almost seven percent on early-returned ballots. He made the claim despite recent polls that favor Democratic opponent Abdul El‑Sayed.
author: The Hill

title: Election officials concerned as DOJ monitors Tuesday's polling stations
content: Election officials have expressed worry that the Department of Justice will monitor polling stations for Tuesday’s vote, after some were notified of the planned oversight. NPR voting correspondent Miles Parks says he will be observing the election day process and the subsequent aftermath.
summary: Some election officials have been notified that the DOJ will monitor their polling stations. NPR voting correspondent Miles Parks says he will watch the vote on election day and afterward.
author: NPR Politics

title: Democrats contest Kentucky midterm race in Trump‑leaning district
content: Democrats are contesting midterm races in districts that President Donald Trump carried by double‑digit margins in 2024. Kentucky Public Radio’s Sylvia Goodman discusses what the results from a single Kentucky district might indicate for Democratic prospects in similar Trump‑stronghold areas.
summary: Democrats are putting up a fight in midterm races this year that went for President Donald Trump by double digits in 2024. Kentucky Public Radio's Sylvia Goodman explains what we can learn from one Kentucky district.
author: NPR Politics

title: Giant algal virus contains tandem potassium channel gene, illuminating protein evolution
content: Researchers have identified a gene encoding a tandem potassium channel in an algal virus. The discovery is presented as evidence that giant viruses may have played a substantial role in the evolution of complex proteins. The study appears in the journal Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
summary: Researchers discovered a gene for a tandem potassium channel in an algal virus. The authors say the finding supports the view that giant viruses may have contributed significantly to the evolution of complex proteins, and the study was published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
author: Phys.org

title: Nighttime bat surveys aid science and reshape public perception
content:
People often react with curiosity when they hear a chirping sound on a detector or feel something whiz past, moments that signal an encounter with microbats. The title notes that seeking these animals after dark can aid scientific research and shift public perception of the creatures.

Microbats are described as small, primarily nocturnal mammals that navigate and hunt using ultrasonic echolocation. They emit calls and listen to the returning echoes to locate objects and prey.
summary: Researchers conduct after‑dark searches for microbats, which are small nocturnal mammals that navigate and hunt using ultrasonic echolocation. The resulting data can advance scientific knowledge and change how people view these animals.
author: Phys.org

title: NES Contra 1987 ported from assembly to C and WebAssembly with online co‑op
content:
A Show HN post announces a browser‑based port of the 1987 NES game Contra. The author used vermiceli’s annotated disassembly of the original ROM as a reference, translating the 6502 assembly routine by routine into C and verifying each frame against the original using the Mesen emulator. The resulting C code was then compiled to WebAssembly, allowing the game to run in a web browser.

The port adds online multiplayer, enabling two players to cooperate over the internet. The project’s source code is hosted on GitHub, and the submission has received 28 points and 17 comments on Hacker News.
summary: The 1987 NES game Contra was translated routine‑by‑routine from its 6502 assembly into C and then compiled to WebAssembly to run in a browser. The port adds online multiplayer so two players can play co‑op over the internet.
author: Hacker News

title: HackerTube offers YouTube-style UI with 6,454 videos from Hacker News comments
content: HackerTube is a YouTube‑style interface that presents 6,454 videos drawn from 39,834 Hacker News comments dating back to 2007. The site is available at https://hackertube.org, and the project was discussed on Hacker News (item 50319510) where the thread has earned 382 points and 148 comments.
summary: HackerTube provides a YouTube‑style UI featuring 6,454 videos. The videos are sourced from 39,834 Hacker News comments since 2007.
author: Hacker News

title: TechCrunch Founder Summit on Nov 4 in Boston offers networking to scale startups
content: With only four days remaining, the TechCrunch Founder Summit is set for November 4 at Boston’s SoWa Power Station. The event promises a full day of meaningful networking, actionable insights and connections that could alter the trajectory of participants’ ideas and startups. Attendees are urged to register now before door‑price increases take effect.
summary: The TechCrunch Founder Summit will take place on November 4 at Boston’s SoWa Power Station. Attendees can expect a full day of networking, actionable insights and startup‑scaling connections, and are urged to register before prices increase at the door.

title: Police clash with Gen Z protesters across Germany demanding education funding
content: Police and protesters clashed on Saturday in Germany as tens of thousands of young people took to the streets. The demonstrations were organized by a collective called “GenZ regelt!” (“Gen Z has got this!”) and were inspired by similar movements in other European countries. Participants marched across the country to demand increased funding for education and to protest the high cost of living. The confrontations involved police responding to the large-scale protests.
summary: Police and protesters clashed on Saturday in Germany as tens of thousands of young people took to the streets. The demonstrations, organized by the collective "GenZ regelt!", called for more education funding and protested the high cost of living.
author: France 24

title: Around 320,000 protest living costs in France in largely peaceful third rally
content: Around 320,000 protesters participated in a third mass protest over living costs across France on Saturday, according to the interior ministry, while organizers counted nearly half a million. Authorities said most demonstrations were largely peaceful, although tensions flared at the end of marches in some cities.
summary: Around 320,000 protesters participated in a third mass protest over living costs across France on Saturday, according to the interior ministry. Organizers said nearly half a million took part, and authorities reported most demonstrations were largely peaceful though tensions flared at the end of marches in some cities.
author: France 24

title: Serbia's Student List wins as Vucic's power apparatus disintegrates
content: After the Student List secured an election victory, observers note that Aleksandar Vučić’s power apparatus is disintegrating. The public is calling for justice promptly, while opponents of the former administration continue to wield influence within the judiciary and administrative bodies.
summary: The Student List won an election, prompting signs that Aleksandar Vucic's power apparatus is disintegrating. However, opponents still control the judiciary and administration, and people are demanding swift justice.

title: Samarkand's Registan faces tourism surge as living Silk Road museum
content: As the sun sets over Samarkand’s majestic Registan, its last rays glint across the turquoise mosaics. Dusk settles on the ancient square where great trade routes have crossed for centuries.
summary: Samarkand's Registan faces tourism surge as living Silk Road museum.

title: UN rights chief demands probe of Yemeni staffer’s death after two years in Houthi custody
content: The UN human rights chief on Saturday called for an independent investigation into the death of a Yemeni colleague who had been held by the Houthis for more than two years. His family was informed of his death only weeks after it occurred.
summary: The UN human rights chief on Saturday demanded an independent investigation into the death of a Yemeni colleague who had been held by the Houthis for more than two years. The colleague’s family learned of his death only weeks after it happened.

title: Belfast man charged with explosives and prohibited weapon after raids
content:
A 35‑year‑old man has been charged in Belfast under the Explosives Act and the Firearms Order after police conducted searches of properties on Shankill Road and Edwina Street.  

The charges include two counts of possessing explosives under suspicious circumstances and possession of a prohibited weapon described as a discharge of electricity or noxious gas.
summary: A 35‑year‑old man was charged under the Explosives Act and Firearms Order after police searched properties on Shankill Road and Edwina Street in Belfast. He faces two counts of possessing explosives under suspicious circumstances and a count of possessing a prohibited weapon that discharges electricity or noxious gas.
author: Guardian World

title: Oleshky evacuees reunite at northern Ukraine border after temporary ceasefire
content: BBC reporter Dan Johnson traveled to the northern Ukrainian border with Belarus after evacuated Oleshky residents arrived in buses and ambulances following a temporary ceasefire. The arrival prompted emotional reunions with loved ones for the Oleshky evacuees.
summary: Dan Johnson of the BBC travelled to the northern Ukrainian border with Belarus after evacuated Oleshky residents arrived in buses and ambulances. The arrivals came after a temporary ceasefire.
author: BBC World

title: West Brom beat West Ham 3-1 as Nuno faces growing pressure
content:
West Ham manager Nuno Espirito Santo faces increasing pressure after his team suffered a second consecutive home defeat, losing 3-1 to West Brom at the London Stadium. The loss leaves the Championship promotion favourites six points behind the leaders in eighth place. Fans expressed their anger toward Nuno at the final whistle, while West Brom’s 3,000 travelling supporters enjoyed the victory.

West Brom, described as slick and measured, moved into the top four with the win. Nuno, who previously managed arch-rivals Wolves, faced significant criticism from the crowd. In other Championship matches, Swansea secured a 4-0 victory, while Middlesbrough cruised past Charlton.
summary: West Brom secured a 3-1 victory at the London Stadium, moving into the Championship top four. West Ham, the promotion favorites, dropped to eighth place and manager Nuno Espirito Santo faced fan anger after his second consecutive home defeat.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Packers' Josh Jacobs faces new abuse allegations from three women in police records
content: Three women contacted police after Jacobs’ May arrest One alleged the Packers star threatened to kill her Lawyers call allegations ‘uncorroborated’ and ‘old’ As police investigated the battery case involving Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs following a May altercation with his then-girlfriend, multiple other women contacted them to detail their own allegations against him. Those accounts were included in evidence regarding Jacobs’ battery case that the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department released on Friday night in response to a public records request. Green Bay TV station NBC 26 first reported the records’ release.
summary: Three women contacted police with allegations against Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs while investigators examined his May battery case. The released police records include claims that Jacobs threatened to kill one of the women, though his lawyers describe the allegations as uncorroborated and old.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Manchester United's 2-0 defeat to Chelsea highlights club dysfunction
content:
Manchester United suffered a 2-0 defeat to Chelsea, a result that has intensified scrutiny on manager Michael Carrick. The article notes that while Carrick is described as being close to dismissal, the broader issue lies in the club’s ongoing dysfunction. The defeat highlights a persistent pattern of losing matches, raising questions about whether the team will continue to struggle under the current manager or the next one.

The piece emphasizes that the depth of the club’s problems is such that the managerial change matters little. This "ambient levels of sadness" suggest that the identity and stability of Manchester United are severely compromised, with the recent loss serving as a symptom of a larger, unresolved crisis within the organization.
summary: Manchester United suffered a 2-0 defeat to Chelsea, raising questions about how long they will continue to lose under current manager Michael Carrick. The article suggests this loss is a minor story compared to the broader dysfunction and sadness at the club.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Breeders’ Cup Turf Sprint features Bacio, winner of Royal Ascot and Nunthorpe
content:
The Breeders’ Cup 2026 day two coverage is underway at Keeneland, with the first race scheduled for 5:10 pm GMT. The focus has shifted to the Breeders’ Cup Turf Sprint, a Grade One contest over five and a half furlongs. Wesley Ward’s horse, Bacio, is highlighted as the primary obstacle to a European clean sweep on the grass.

Bacio is recognized by European racing followers for his August victories in the Palace of Holyroodhouse Handicap at Royal Ascot and the Nunthorpe at York.
summary: The Breeders’ Cup Turf Sprint, a Grade One race over 5½ furlongs, was run on day two of the 2026 Breeders’ Cup at Keeneland. The race featured Wesley Ward’s Bacio, who previously won the Palace of Holyroodhouse Handicap at Royal Ascot and the Nunthorpe at York.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Pakistan clinch tri-series final as Fakhar Zaman scores 127 to beat Sri Lanka
content:
Pakistan clinched the tri‑series title in a dramatic final at Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium. The packed-out venue saw the match settled in the penultimate over, with Pakistan defeating Sri Lanka by three wickets to win the tournament under the lights.

In the chase of 326, Fakhar Zaman delivered the headline performance, smashing 127 off 99 balls. After his dismissal the new batsmen had to remain composed, and the partnership that followed proved decisive.

Arafat Minhas (21) and Hasan Nawaz (24) forged a 94‑run stand that secured the win. Minhas and Faheem Ashraf were dismissed with two runs still required, but Shaheen Afridi finished the evening with a powerful boundary over the ropes. Sri Lankan opener Kamindu Mendis also scored 131, but his efforts could not prevent Pakistan’s victory.
summary: Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by three wickets in the tri-series final at Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore, chasing 326. Fakhar Zaman made 127 off 99 balls, supported by a 94‑run partnership from Arafat Minhas and Hasan Nawaz, and Shaheen Afridi hit the winning runs.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Glasner defiant as Brentford exploit Nottingham Forest woes
content: For Oliver Glasner and Nottingham Forest, the future starts now. His post-match press conference lasted 14 frustrated minutes in which, repeatedly banging the desk, he blamed himself for compromising his principles and told players that if they didn’t “buy in” they could “leave”. “For me, I go home and have breakfast with my family, so it’s not the worst situation,” Glasner said. “Nobody needs to have pity with Oliver Glasner. If I want, I could start in two weeks somewhere else. I won’t do it. But the players, the staff, they remain in the same situation. And it’s the same shit situation than the club had last year. So you need to change and rebuild from the bottom to the top. And this is clear for me. And this is what I will do. And without any compromises, zero, zero.”
summary: Oliver Glasner held a 14-minute press conference where he blamed himself for compromising principles and told Nottingham Forest players to leave if they did not buy in. He stated that the club must change and rebuild from the bottom to the top without any compromises.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Brighton Defeat Manchester City 1-0 as Yasin Ayari Scores Winner
content:
Brighton secured a victory over Manchester City on Saturday, with Yasin Ayari scoring the 11th-minute winner. The goal resulted from a free-kick awarded for a “foul” by Brighton’s Elliot Anderson on Ayari, a decision that appeared wrongly made. This result extends Manchester City’s losing streak to two consecutive league matches.

Following the win, Brighton’s manager Fabian Hürzeler’s team is positioned third in the league standings. The article notes that Brighton can be proud of this achievement and their current standing, suggesting they are worth their lofty position and capable of qualifying for the Champions League.
summary: Brighton defeated Manchester City 1-0 on Saturday thanks to an 11th-minute goal by Yasin Ayari. The victory moves Brighton into third place in the league standings.

title: Binance recovers 90 percent of stolen assets from hack
content:
Binance announced on Saturday that it had recovered 90 percent of the assets stolen in a $6.3 billion hack of its platform. The exchange said the missing funds were replenished after the theft.

On Thursday, the stolen money began moving out of Binance wallets, leading the company to suspend all deposits and withdrawals. In response, some other cryptocurrency firms froze roughly $3 billion in assets connected to the incident.
summary: Binance said on Saturday it had replenished 90 percent of assets stolen in a $6.3 billion hack. The company suspended all deposits and withdrawals after the money began moving out of its wallets on Thursday.

title: UChicago researchers find radiation-activated TET2 locks immune cells in suppressive state
content:
Researchers at the University of Chicago have identified a mechanism to reverse the immune suppression caused by radiation therapy in cancer patients. Their study, published in Cancer Cell, shows that radiation activates a protein called TET2 in bone‑marrow immune cells.  

TET2 removes chemical tags from RNA, locking these cells into an immune‑suppressing state. By targeting this pathway, the researchers suggest the possibility of reprogramming the cells so they attack tumors instead of protecting them.
summary: Researchers at the University of Chicago identified a mechanism by which radiation therapy reprograms immune cells to protect tumors rather than attack them. The Cancer Cell study shows radiation activates the protein TET2 in bone‑marrow immune cells, removing RNA chemical tags and locking the cells into an immune‑suppressing state.
author: Medical Xpress

content: Four superconducting cables link two large quantum processors into one. Researchers believe that building quantum computers in multiple interconnected parts is the best path forward, allowing separate processors to work together as a larger machine. The connections must carry fragile quantum information without destroying it.
summary: Four superconducting cables connect two large quantum processors into a single system. The connections must carry fragile quantum information without destroying it.

title: Ultracold atoms simulate hard-to-observe matter‑antimatter pair production
content: Ultracold atoms are used to simulate matter‑antimatter pair production, a process that is difficult to observe directly. According to quantum electrodynamics, a sufficiently strong electric field can, in principle, convert its energy into particles and their antimatter partners. The antimatter partner shares the same mass and, for electrically charged particles, carries the opposite electric charge.
summary: Quantum electrodynamics predicts that a sufficiently strong electric field can convert energy into particles and their antimatter partners. In such pairs, the antimatter partner has the same mass and opposite electric charge.
author: Phys.org

content:
The distinction between native, introduced, and invasive species can be life‑or‑death.  
In Australia, invasive species such as European rabbits and feral pigs are often culled, while most native animals are generally left alone.
summary: Distinctions between "native," "introduced" and "invasive" species can often be life or death. In Australia, species considered invasive, such as European rabbits and feral pigs, are often culled, while most native animals are generally left alone.

content: Chemists have created an AI tool that converts human ingenuity into life‑enhancing enzymes. Assistant professor Zhongyue (John) Yang, former doctoral student Qianzhen Shao—now a postdoc at Stanford—and other team members developed the system, which is designed to elevate scientists’ work rather than replace it.

content: A woman experienced a severe allergic reaction after sexual contact, caused by an antibiotic present in her partner’s semen. The incident has prompted clinicians to recommend that this risk be added to the antibiotic’s patient information leaflet.
summary: A woman experienced a severe allergic reaction to an antibiotic present in her partner's semen after sex. Clinicians are urging that this risk be added to the antibiotic's patient information leaflet.

title: Boot Sector Language Model Generates Infinite Linux Boot Logs
content:
A new language model project has been showcased on Hacker News, featuring an inference engine that fits entirely within a 510-byte Master Boot Record (MBR). The project draws inspiration from the boot sector demo scene, where developers previously created applications such as chess games and C compilers in 512 bytes. This neural network generates Linux boot logs for non-existent hardware by producing dmesg messages infinitely. The system utilizes a small character-level network trained on dmesg data, with the weights, vocabulary, and strings stored in the sectors immediately following the MBR.

During development, the creator identified a specific bug by comparing the output of a Python simulator with the assembly code running in QEMU. Although the initial characters matched, the output eventually diverged. By retrieving hidden layer values via QEMU’s debug port, it was determined that only the first neuron was calculated correctly. The issue stemmed from the idiv instruction, which stores its remainder in the edx register, overwriting the pointer to the biases table. This caused the first neuron to be biased correctly while subsequent neurons used garbage data. The fix involved determining the bias address from the loop counter to ensure no pointers survived the division operation.

A second bug was discovered by inspecting the code before the initial run. The BIOS print routine zeros out the bx register, which contained the predicted character number. This necessitated the use of push and pop instructions to preserve the value of bx around the print call. The project contrasts with Sectorllm, which runs a 5-layer Llama2 model with an attention mechanism in 1.2K of assembly code. In contrast, this project prioritizes fitting the engine into a single sector, resulting in a network with just one hidden layer of int8 operations.
summary: A 510‑byte MBR contains an inference engine that uses a small char‑level neural network to generate Linux boot messages infinitely. The author debugged integer‑arithmetic bugs, fixing bias pointer and BIOS print routine issues to match QEMU output.
author: Hacker News

title: Astronomers Find White Dwarfs Can Appear Pink, Green and Other Colors
content: Astronomers have discovered that white dwarfs can display colors beyond white, including pink and green. The study shows that a white dwarf’s density and the type of material it has absorbed from its surroundings can produce a rainbow of shades in the star’s atmosphere.
summary: Scientists discovered that white dwarfs can turn pink and green. They found that a white dwarf’s density and the material it absorbs from its surroundings can produce a rainbow of shades in its atmosphere.
author: Wired

title: Scientists Replicate 1960s Planarian Memory Transfer Study
content: Scientists are revisiting a controversial 1960s experiment in which planarian worms appeared to transfer memories after one worm ate another, a result that was hailed as sensational until the worms later ceased learning. The new replication effort aims to determine whether memories can indeed be transferred.
summary: In the 1960s, an experiment showed planarian worms could transfer memories by consuming each other. The finding was later questioned when the worms stopped learning.
author: Wired

title: Creator builds $50 AI Muse Charm Tamagotchi before Meta's version
content:
Meta is promoting a device called the Muse Charm, described as a “jolly AI helper” that can be carried like a Tamagotchi and features a squishy, cute face. The company plans to sell the Muse Charm during the holiday season.

One writer notes that they built a similar AI‑enabled device before Meta’s offering. Their version, which cost $50, does not include a camera or a 5G cellular radio but can communicate with Muse, display cute avatars, function as a pocket watch, and serve as a remote camera viewfinder. The author also says the device could theoretically control a smart home if additional code is added.

The writer declines to purchase Meta’s Muse Charm, preferring the home‑built version they consider a worthwhile learning experience.
summary: The author assembled a $50 home‑made AI device called a Muse Charm that talks to Muse and displays cute avatars. It lacks cameras and 5G, functions as a pocket watch and remote camera viewfinder, and could theoretically control a smart home with added code.
author: The Verge

title: Nintendo announces first annual Pikmin Day and new Pikmin 4 features for Switch 2
content:
Nintendo announced that November 1 will mark the first annual Pikmin Day. The company’s Pikmin Day Direct, presented by Shigeru Miyamoto, revealed new details about the upcoming Pikmin 4 on the Switch 2, an update for the mobile game Pikmin Bloom, and the launch of a Hello! Pikmin series of shorts.

The presentation also confirmed that Switch 2 owners can use the console’s built‑in microphone to give voice commands to Oatchi, the space dog, and that Pikmin 4 will include a Dandori Academy mode featuring specific skill challenges. Limited test sessions will run on Friday, Saturday and Sunday, with leaderboards for players to compare their results.
summary: This morning, Nintendo announced that tomorrow, November 1st, would be the first annual Pikmin Day. As part of the short Pikmin Day Direct, Shigeru Miyamoto shared new info about Pikmin 4 for the Switch 2, as well as an update for the mobile app Pikmin Bloom, and announced the Hello!
author: The Verge

title: Binance CEO says 90% of $6.3B stolen assets have been replenished
content:
Binance disclosed that hackers stole approximately $6.3 billion from its customers in what it described as a record‑breaking crypto heist. The company’s chief executive said the firm has already replenished about 90 percent of the stolen assets and intends to cover the remaining 10 percent, which consists of “less liquid” tokens that may take longer to acquire.

Binance added that withdrawals remain paused but are expected to resume on Sunday, reiterating its commitment to fully absorb the financial impact of the incident.
summary: Binance CEO said the firm has replaced 90 percent of the $6.3 billion taken from customers and will cover the remaining 10 percent, which consists of less‑liquid tokens that may take longer to acquire. Withdrawals remain paused but are expected to be reenabled on Sunday.
author: The Verge

title: France limits two anti‑racism rallies near Paris to eastern outskirts
content:
Two rallies against racism are scheduled to take place near Paris, according to the report’s headline. The events are set against a broader wave of unrest, as France prepares for a third weekend of protests over the rising cost of living. Authorities anticipate nearly half a million participants nationwide and have mobilized 70,000 police officers to maintain order.

In Paris, a last‑minute court ruling has limited today’s march to the city’s eastern outskirts. The coverage of these developments is provided by Jack Pownall.
summary: France is preparing for a third weekend of protests over the rising cost of living, with nearly half a million people expected nationwide and 70,000 police deployed. A last‑minute court ruling restricted the two anti‑racism rallies near Paris to the city’s eastern outskirts.
author: France 24

title: French Interior Minister fears disorder after dark on Halloween
content:
Saturday will see another day of nationwide demonstrations over the cost of living and school conditions, described as “Act Three” and uniting Yellow Vest activists with student demonstrators. France’s highest administrative court has upheld a ban on the planned Paris march route, requiring protesters to stay on the city’s eastern outskirts.

Authorities are deploying 70,000 security personnel and imposing curfews in some areas, echoing measures used last weekend. The interior minister issued a Halloween‑themed warning that covering one’s face at a demonstration remains illegal, according to Ophelie Jacobson.
summary: Saturday is set to see another day of nationwide demonstrations over the cost of living and conditions in schools. Dubbed “Act Three”, the protests bring together Yellow Vest activists and student demonstrators.
author: France 24

title: European ministers confront Russia's Lavrov and skip group photo at G20
content:
The G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in the United States is concluding two days of talks without reaching agreement on several key global security issues. On the sidelines, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio signed an Arctic cooperation agreement with Japan and South Korea and confirmed Washington’s participation in Riyadh’s World Expo in 2030.

European ministers confronted Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov over the war in Ukraine and declined to join him for the traditional group photo, highlighting the division caused by Russia’s presence at the summit. Jack Pownall reports.
summary: The G20 foreign ministers’ meeting in the US is wrapping up two days of talks without agreement on several key global security issues. On the sidelines, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio signed an Arctic cooperation deal with Japan and South Korea and confirmed Washington’s participation in Riyadh’s World Expo in 2030.
author: France 24

title: Dozens protest at Poland's Constitutional Tribunal, several detained
content: Police in Poland increased security around the Constitutional Tribunal after dozens of protesters gathered on Friday to oppose the government’s suspension of its president, a move the demonstrators claim is unlawful. Several people were detained after some protesters breached the court’s perimeter fence, according to police. Charlotte Hughes reports.
summary: Police increased security around the Constitutional Tribunal after dozens of protesters gathered on Friday to oppose the government's suspension of its president, which they called unlawful. Police said several people were detained after some demonstrators breached the court's perimeter fence.
author: France 24

title: UK PM Andy Burnham open to slavery apology, rejects financial reparations
content: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Saturday he was “open” to the UK issuing its first apology for its role in the trans‑Atlantic slave trade, but he rejected calls for financial reparations. The debate comes as King Charles continues his visit to three Caribbean nations ahead of the Commonwealth summit.
summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said on Saturday he was “open” to the UK apologising for its role in the transatlantic slave trade but rejected calls for financial reparations. The issue has featured prominently during King Charles’s ongoing visit to three Caribbean nations ahead of a Commonwealth summit.
author: France 24

title: Oleshky Residents Reunite with Families After Rescue Operation
content: On Saturday, evacuees from the Russian‑occupied city of Oleshky crossed into Ukrainian‑held territory during a major rescue operation. They had traveled through Belarus amid a rare truce brokered by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump. Oleshky has been under Russian occupation since 2022, and intense fighting left residents starving and unable to leave.
summary: Evacuees from Oleshky crossed into Ukrainian‑held territory Saturday in a major rescue operation after traveling through Belarus during a rare truce brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump. The city has been under Russian occupation since 2022 and was caught in intense fighting that left residents starving and unable to leave.
author: France 24

title: Khamenei warns US and Israel against new attacks amid Middle East tensions
content: Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei issued a warning on Saturday, telling the United States and Israel not to carry out additional strikes as concerns grow about renewed fighting in the Middle East. The warning follows recent threats of military action against Iran made by U.S. President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump has not yet decided on any new strikes.
summary: Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned the United States and Israel on Saturday against further strikes. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Donald Trump had not yet decided on fresh attacks.
author: France 24

title: Government corruption tops concerns of US midterm voters, poll shows
content:
A recent exclusive poll indicates that government corruption has emerged as a top issue for voters heading into the US midterm elections. The article highlights that alleged self-dealing by the president and his allies is becoming a significant concern for the electorate. This shift in voter sentiment contrasts with historical political narratives, such as the “welfare queen” trope popularized by Ronald Reagan in 1976, which focused on fraud by the poor rather than high-level governmental misconduct.

The text details several specific allegations of financial entanglements involving the Trump administration and its associates. It notes that the Qatari government gifted the president a luxury jet, a move that potentially violates the emoluments clause of the constitution. Additionally, the UAE reportedly gained access to high-end American AI chips shortly after an investment firm linked to its ruling family purchased a $500 million stake in World Liberty Financial, a crypto company funded by the families of Trump and Steve Witkoff.

Further examples of alleged self-dealing include the pardons granted to Wanda Vázquez Garced, the former governor of Puerto Rico, and Julio Herrera Velutini, a banker who paid her bribes. These pardons followed a $50 million deal between Velutini’s family and Alina Habba, Trump’s former personal lawyer, as well as a $3.5 million donation to Trump’s Maga Inc Super Pac. The article also points to the Pentagon lending over $600 million to Vulcan Elements, a rare earths startup, three months after Donald Jr’s venture capital firm, 1789 Capital, acquired a stake in the company.

Finally, the piece mentions Powerus, a drone maker backed by Eric and Donald Trump, which is selling drone interceptors to Persian Gulf allies. The source characterizes this as enriching the president’s children from a war launched without consulting Congress. These incidents collectively form the basis for the growing voter concern regarding corruption in the government.
summary: An exclusive poll found that government corruption is a top issue for US midterm voters. The report cites alleged self‑dealing by President Trump and his allies, including a Qatari‑gifted luxury jet, UAE access to American AI chips after a stake purchase, and donations linked to pardons.
author: Guardian World

title: Judge rules firing of assistant US attorney Maurene Comey unlawful
content:
Legal experts praised a recent decision that blocked the dismissal of Maurene Comey, an assistant U.S. attorney, while cautioning that an appeal is probable. Judge Jesse Furman ruled this week that the Justice Department’s termination of Comey “without cause” was unlawful, a judgment that veterans said could send a strong message about politicized firings and affect other judges handling similar cases.

Maurene Comey, the daughter of former FBI director James Comey, previously handled high‑profile prosecutions in the Southern District of New York, securing guilty verdicts against Ghislaine Maxwell and Sean “Diddy” Combs. The ruling is being viewed as a potential check on efforts perceived as attacks on the rule of law.
summary: Judge Jesse Furman this week ruled that the Department of Justice’s firing of assistant US attorney Maurene Comey without cause was unlawful. Legal experts said the decision could send a strong message about politicized firings and may be appealed.
author: Guardian World

title: Over 50.5 million early votes cast with three days left before US midterms
content:
More than 50.5 million Americans have cast early ballots as of Saturday morning, three days before the U.S. midterm elections, according to an analysis by the University of Florida. The tally represents a record number of early votes and is nearly five million higher than the total early votes recorded in the 2022 midterms.

The surge in early voting is occurring amid a series of tight contests that will determine control of Congress. In the states that collect party‑affiliation data, Democrats have outnumbered Republicans among early voters.
summary: More than 50.5 million early votes have been cast across the United States as of Saturday morning, according to a University of Florida analysis. That total is nearly 5 million higher than the early voting total in the 2022 midterm election and Democrats outnumber Republicans in states that report party data.
author: Guardian World

title: Virginia and DC file federal lawsuit to block Trump memorial arch as construction looms
content:
Legal challenges to Donald Trump’s proposed memorial arch are mounting, with the District of Columbia and Virginia filing a federal lawsuit on Saturday. The administration says construction could begin as early as next week.  

There are now three lawsuits seeking to halt work on a monument that would rise 250 ft (76 m) on a grass patch off the bridge spanning the Potomac River, which connects the city with Arlington National Cemetery. The arch would be 100 ft (30 m) taller than the Statue of Liberty from its base to the torch.
summary: The District of Columbia and Virginia filed a federal lawsuit on Saturday seeking to stop Donald Trump’s proposed 250‑foot memorial arch. The administration says construction could begin as early as next week, and the arch would be 100 feet taller than the Statue of Liberty from its base to the torch.
author: Guardian World

title: Police clash with masked rioters in Paris and Marseille after large French protests
content:
Clashes erupted in Paris, Marseille, and other French cities following a third wave of protests concerning the cost of living and deteriorating public services. According to the interior ministry, approximately 320,000 people participated in rallies nationwide, a decrease from the estimated 410,000 attendees the previous weekend. In Paris, 70,000 demonstrators, some wearing Halloween costumes, marched along boulevards on the south-eastern outskirts, deliberately avoiding the city centre.

Simultaneous demonstrations occurred in Germany, where police deployed teargas to disperse crowds as evening approached. The French protests marked the third consecutive weekend of unrest, with masked rioters engaging in clashes with police forces in several major cities.
summary: Police clash with masked rioters in Paris and Marseille after large French protests.
author: Guardian World

title: Oleshky evacuees reunite with families after truce permits crossing into Ukraine
content:
Evacuees from the Russian‑occupied city of Oleshky crossed into Ukrainian‑held territory on Saturday and were reunited with their families. The crossing occurred under a truce described as the most significant since Russia’s full‑scale invasion began four and a half years ago, and the major rescue operation that enabled it started on Friday.

Residents of nearby villages lined the highway, waving flags to greet the convoy as it entered the area. The operation facilitated the movement of the Oleshky evacuees across the front line during the brief cease‑fire.
summary: Evacuees from the Russian‑occupied city of Oleshky crossed into Ukrainian‑held territory on Saturday and were reunited with their families. The major rescue operation began on Friday and was carried out under the most significant truce since Russia’s full‑scale invasion of Ukraine four and a half years ago.
author: Guardian World

title: Artists in Albanese's Grayndler seat rally against AI content-scraping proposal
content: Inner west Sydney seat has long been safely held by the PM – but potential changes to copyright laws are angering its large creative community Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast The prime minister is facing growing discontent within his own electorate as creatives push back against the federal government’s proposal to allow AI companies to scrape everything Australians create online. Anthony Albanese’s seat of Grayndler in Sydney’s inner west is home to more than 3,000 cultural and creative businesses, and 10% of its workers are employed in cultural and creative fields – compared with 4.2% nationally.
summary: Creative workers in the Grayndler electorate are pushing back against the federal government's proposal to allow AI companies to scrape everything Australians create online. The seat, held by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, includes more than 3,000 cultural and creative businesses and has 10% of its workers employed in cultural and creative fields.
author: Guardian World
